WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT

how-we-work.title: How we work

how-we-work.html:
HOW WE WORK

One team.
From idea to impact.

Good delivery comes from shared understanding, clear ownership and frequent, honest communication.

UK CLIENT LEADERSHIP

Context.
Accountability.
Partnership.

＋
AFRICAN ENGINEERING

Ingenuity.
Craft.
Commitment.

THE DELIVERY JOURNEY

Clarity at every step.

01

Discover

Understand the problem, users, constraints and measures of success.

02

Define

Agree scope, architecture, delivery approach and responsibilities.

03

Deliver

Build in visible increments, with reviews, testing and shared decisions.

04

Evolve

Launch with a handover, support plan and prioritised next steps.

WAYS TO WORK TOGETHER

A model that fits the work.

Discovery & advisory

A focused engagement to turn uncertainty into an actionable plan.

Project delivery

An agreed scope delivered by a dedicated team, with milestones and acceptance criteria.

Dedicated teams

Additional engineering capacity integrated with your people, tools and priorities.

CONFIDENCE BY DESIGN

Know what to expect.

Explore the responsibilities and quality practices we agree before delivery.

Explore delivery assurance↗
Compare engagement models↗

GOOD QUESTIONS

Working together,
made clear.

Who will I work with?＋

We agree a named delivery lead and a team suited to the work before the engagement starts. UK coordination connects your stakeholders with the engineering team.

How do you handle time zones?＋

We agree shared working hours, review sessions and escalation routes at the start. The aim is meaningful collaboration with room for focused engineering.

How do you approach security and IP?＋

Access, confidentiality, intellectual property, data handling and any cross-border requirements are agreed contractually before delivery. Controls must match the specific project.

Can you work with our existing technology?＋

We assess your stack and requirements first, then propose engineers with relevant skills. We will be clear about any capability gaps or specialist partners needed.

Do you use AI-assisted coding?＋

Where appropriate, with client agreement. Engineers remain responsible for architecture, review, testing, security and the final deliverable. Sensitive client material must only be used with approved tools and settings.

LET’S MAKE PROGRESS

Your next chapter.
Built together.

Bring us your challenge. We’ll help you find a practical way forward.

Let’s talk about your project ↗

about.title: About SIT Consultancy
about.description: Meet SIT Consultancy: UK leadership, engineering talent in Liberia and across Africa, shared principles and a connected approach to software, AI, data and cloud.
about.html:
ABOUT SIT CONSULTANCY

Different perspectives.
One shared ambition.

UK leadership. African engineering. Technology built around the people it needs to serve.

We bring consulting, software, data and AI together to help organisations turn a meaningful challenge into a practical way forward.

Meet your next technology partner↗View company capabilities↗
Get to know SITOur storyConnected deliveryOur principlesYour questions

WHY WE’RE BUILDING SIT

Good technology starts
with understanding people.

Ambitious organisations need more than technical capacity. They need people who understand the challenge, ask useful questions and take responsibility for the work.

Headquartered in the United Kingdom, with developers in Africa including Liberia, SIT Consultancy brings people together around meaningful work. Our focus is practical: understand your challenge, assemble the relevant expertise and shape an approach your organisation can work with.

We believe the best partnerships create lasting capability. That means sharing knowledge, developing engineers and helping your team own what we build together.

Headquarters
United Kingdom
Engineering talent
Liberia & across Africa
Our focus
Software, AI, data & cloud

THE PEOPLE BEHIND THE WORK

Different locations.
One connected team.

Business understanding and engineering craft belong in the same conversation. Here’s how we bring them together.

Close to the decisions that matter.

UK client leadership connects the business challenge to a practical delivery plan. We agree who owns priorities, who approves decisions and how progress will be reviewed.

  • A named point of contact for the engagement
  • Clear scope, responsibilities and review points
Compare ways to work↗

Technical talent. Shared ownership.

Developers in Liberia and across Africa bring engineering capability to the work. Team composition, relevant skills and availability are agreed around your project—not a generic list of technologies.

  • Skills matched to the proposed scope
  • Working increments, review and documentation
Explore our technology toolkit↗

Distance should not create uncertainty.

Before work begins, we agree shared working hours, communication channels, access and escalation. Your team stays involved through demonstrations, decisions and a clear handover.

  • An agreed collaboration and review rhythm
  • Knowledge transfer and operating ownership
Explore our delivery model↗

Responsibilities, shared hours and delivery terms are agreed for your engagement.

How we build confidence↗

WHAT GUIDES US

Principles you can see
in the way we work.

Clear thinking, thoughtful engineering and a commitment to leave your team stronger.

01

Be clear

Make the important things visible.

Agree scope, explain trade-offs and raise uncertainty early. Progress should be understandable to the people making decisions.

02

Care about the craft

Start with a real problem

privacy.html:
YOUR INFORMATION

Privacy, made clear.

A working privacy notice for this initial website release.

About this preview

The private design preview does not send or store project enquiries. Please use sample information while exploring the form.

When the WordPress site is configured

The request form collects your name, work email, organisation, challenge description, request type, service interest, indicative budget, timeline and your consent to respond. Depending on your request, it also collects your preferred conversation format, time zone and availability; project stage and product type; or required roles, team size and engagement duration. Authorised SIT request staff use this information to review and respond to your request.

The form is for general business enquiries. Do not include sensitive personal information, credentials or confidential project material. No marketing subscription is created when you submit an enquiry.

Before public launch

SIT Consultancy must publish its verified contact details, applicable legal basis, retention period, processors, international transfer arrangements and rights contact before enabling live enquiries. The website administrator controls whether enquiries are enabled.

Cookies

This theme does not add advertising or analytics cookies. WordPress and hosting services may use necessary cookies. Any additional tracking requires a reviewed notice and appropriate controls.

Optional project context and downloads

The brief builder can include intended users, existing systems, integrations, desired outcomes and delivery requirements. These optional answers are submitted with your request on the configured WordPress site. Draft downloads are created in your browser when you choose to download; keep that file on a device you control. The form does not automatically save drafts in browser storage.

sample-deliverables/discovery-brief.html:
SAMPLE DELIVERABLE

Discovery brief

Agree the problem before choosing the solution.

Editable example · No client data · Adapt to your project
Download template ↓Print / save PDFAll templates↗

Decision to make

What decision should this discovery enable?
Example: decide whether a self-service request portal is worth piloting.

People and the current journey

Name the sponsor, delivery owner and user groups. Describe the current workflow and the friction to investigate.
Example: staff enter the same request in several systems; validate this through interviews and observation.

Evidence and success

Record the current baseline, how it was measured, and the desired change. Leave targets uncommitted until the baseline is understood.
Evidence to collect: request volumes, handling steps, user feedback and existing system constraints.

Scope and boundaries

In scope: journey research, options, feasibility and a prioritised pilot backlog.
Out of scope until agreed: production build, live data migration and integrations.

Outputs and acceptance

A problem statement, options with trade-offs, risk register, outline architecture and recommended next step.
Acceptance: the sponsor reviews the evidence, records decisions and agrees whether to proceed.

Inputs and open questions

Identify stakeholders, approved system access, budget boundaries and decision dates. Track each unanswered question with an owner and review date.

sample-deliverables/architecture-decisio.html:
SAMPLE DELIVERABLE

Architecture decision record

Make technical choices understandable and reviewable.

Editable example · No client data · Adapt to your project
Download template ↓Print / save PDFAll templates↗

Record

Decision ID: ADR-001
Status: proposed example, not approved
Owner / date / reviewers: to be assigned

Context

An illustrative service needs to notify staff when a request arrives. Requests must remain available if the email provider is temporarily unavailable.

Options

A. Send email in the request handler: fewer components, but provider failure affects the request.
B. Save the request and queue a notification: more operational work, but delivery can be retried.

Proposed decision

Evaluate a transactional outbox so the request and notification intent are stored together. Use a worker with bounded retries and a visible failure state.

Consequences

Benefits: request handling can be independent of provider availability.
Costs: monitor the queue, handle duplicate delivery, define retention and make failed notifications visible.

Verification and revisit triggers

Test rollback, retry, duplicate processing and provider outage. Review this choice if volume, hosting capabilities or delivery requirements change. Record approval before implementation.

Discuss your project↗

sample-deliverables/delivery-roadmap.html:
SAMPLE DELIVERABLE

Delivery roadmap

Connect delivery stages to decisions and acceptance.

Editable example · No client data · Adapt to your project
Download template ↓Print / save PDFAll templates↗

Outcome and owners

Business outcome: to be agreed. Sponsor, product owner, delivery lead and reviewers: to be assigned. This template intentionally makes no schedule or price promise.

Stage 1 — Understand

Activities: user research, system review, baseline and constraints.
Output: agreed discovery brief.
Exit decision: is the proposed outcome valuable and feasible enough to investigate?

Stage 2 — Define

Activities: prototype, architecture options, risk review and backlog.
Output: reviewed delivery plan and acceptance criteria.
Exit decision: agree scope, commercial model and responsibilities.

Stage 3 — Build and review

Activities: work in small increments, test, demonstrate and capture decisions.
Output: reviewable releases and an updated risk/dependency log.
Exit decision: stakeholders accept the agreed release scope.

Stage 4 — Release and transfer

Activities: rehearse migration, verify rollback, train operators and transfer documentation.
Output: release record, runbook and ownership checklist.
Exit decision: named owners approve launch and support arrangements.

Track changes

For each change record the reason, impact on scope/cost/date, approver and decision. Keep unresolved dependencies visible; revise estimates when evidence changes.

sample-deliverables/quality-review.description: Bring review evidence into release decisions. An editable SIT Consultancy sample.
sample-deliverables/quality-review.html:
SAMPLE DELIVERABLE

Quality review checklist

Bring review evidence into release decisions.

Editable example · No client data · Adapt to your project
Download template ↓Print / save PDFAll templates↗

Review context

Release, environment, scope, reviewer and date: to be completed. For each check record Pass / Fail / Not applicable, a reason and a link to evidence. This is a planning aid, not a certification.

Behaviour and resilience

Check agreed acceptance criteria, input validation, permission boundaries, retries, duplicate requests, failure messages, backups and rollback. Confirm that incomplete work cannot be mistaken for success.

Security and data

Review dependency findings, approved data flows, secrets handling, least privilege, logging and retention. Track unresolved findings with an owner and explicit release decision.

Usability and accessibility

Check keyboard operation, focus visibility, readable labels, error recovery, zoom and narrow screens. Include manual checks with assistive technology relevant to the service.

Performance and operations

Measure representative user journeys, document test conditions, verify monitoring and alerts, and agree support ownership. Set budgets appropriate to the project before assessing them.

Release recommendation

Summarise evidence, unresolved risks and acceptance conditions. Name the person accountable for the go/no-go decision and record the decision date.

sample-deliverables/handover-checklist.html:
SAMPLE DELIVERABLE

Handover checklist

Make ownership part of delivery.

Editable example · No client data · Adapt to your project
Download template ↓Print / save PDFAll templates↗

Ownership

Name the business owner, technical owner, support contact and escalation route. Confirm who can approve releases, access changes and supplier costs.

Code and environments

Transfer repository access, build instructions, environment inventory and deployment documentation. Verify the receiving team can build and deploy. Share credentials only through an approved secret-management process.

Runbook

Document routine checks, monitoring, alerts, backup restoration, incident triage and rollback. Rehearse critical recovery steps and record results.

Data and suppliers

Record approved data flows, storage, retention, integrations and supplier dependencies. Confirm account ownership, licences, renewal responsibilities and access removal.

Knowledge transfer

Run a walkthrough of architecture and key workflows. Capture known limitations, unresolved risks and prioritised improvements. Record questions and owners.

Acceptance

List deliverables received, evidence reviewed and exceptions agreed. Record the handover decision, named owners and the start/end of any agreed support period.
